title: Unit rates and rate problems
blurb: Find unit rates and better buys, convert hours and minutes before you divide, and use a rate to find an amount, a time or an average speed.
question: An IV of 1,000 mL runs over 8 hours, a nurse counts 18 heartbeats in 15 seconds, and a driver covers 240 miles at two different speeds. The HESI A2 asks for the rate in mL per hour, the heart rate per minute and the average speed. How do you handle each one?

teach.body: Formally, a rate is a ratio of two quantities measured in DIFFERENT units, such as miles per hour, dollars per pound or mL per hour. A unit rate is the amount for exactly one unit of the second quantity. In plain English: a rate tells you 'this much for each one of that'. The word after 'per' is the one you divide by.

teach.h: Unit rate: divide by the 'per' quantity
teach.body: To find a unit rate, divide the first quantity by the amount of the unit after 'per'. $4.50 for 3 lb: 4.50 ÷ 3 = $1.50 per lb. 150 miles in 2.5 hours: 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 miles per hour. To compare deals, find each unit price in the same unit; the lower unit price is the better buy. If your rate comes out as hours per mile when the question wants miles per hour, you divided the wrong way.

teach.caption: The biggest pack is not always the cheapest per item. Divide each time.

teach.h: Convert the time before you divide
items: Minutes to hours: divide by 60. 15 min = 0.25 h; 30 min = 0.5 h; 45 min = 0.75 h; 40 min = 2/3 h.
260 mL in 3 hours 15 minutes: 3.25 h, so 260 ÷ 3.25 = 80 mL per hour. Check: 80 × 3.25 = 260. ✓
42 miles in 35 minutes: 42 ÷ 35 = 1.2 miles per minute, × 60 = 72 miles per hour.
Seconds to minutes: 60 seconds = 1 minute, so a 15-second count × 4 gives a rate per minute.

teach.text: Three rate slips build most HESI distractors: dividing the wrong way (hours per mile), writing 3 hours 30 minutes as 3.30 hours (it is 3.5), and averaging two speeds. Average speed is total distance ÷ total time, because more time is spent at the slower speed.

teach.h: Average speed for a whole trip

items: An IV of 1,000 mL is ordered over 8 hours. Rate = 1,000 ÷ 8 = 125 mL per hour. Check: 125 × 8 = 1,000. ✓
A nurse counts 18 heartbeats in 15 seconds. A minute has 4 sets of 15 seconds, so 18 × 4 = 72 beats per minute.
Check the heart rate as a unit rate: 18 ÷ 15 = 1.2 beats per second, and 1.2 × 60 = 72. ✓
Always label the units: mL per hour and beats per minute, never just '125' or '72'.

teach.h: Using a rate of 125 mL per hour
teach.caption: Units guide you: (mL per hour) × hours = mL; mL ÷ (mL per hour) = hours.

items: Catching up: 1,000 mL is ordered over 8 hours. After 3 hours, 450 mL have infused. Left: 550 mL in 5 hours.
New rate: 550 ÷ 5 = 110 mL per hour (not the original 125 and not the 150 run so far).
Comparing rates: Clinic A sees 156 patients in 12 hours (13 per hour); Clinic B sees 98 in 7 hours (14 per hour). B sees 1 more per hour.
Decimal hours to minutes: multiply the decimal part by 60. 2.4 h = 2 h + 0.4 × 60 min = 2 h 24 min.
Unit rate = amount ÷ number of 'per' units. Lower unit price = better buy.
Convert minutes to hours (÷ 60) before dividing: 15 min = 0.25 h, not 0.15 h.
Amount = rate × time; time = amount ÷ rate.
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, not the average of the speeds.
Label every rate with its units and check that they make sense.

summary: You can now find unit rates and better buys, convert hours and minutes correctly before dividing, and turn a short count into a rate per minute. You can also use a rate to find an amount or a time, work out a new rate for what is left, and compute an average speed for a whole trip.

A.q: Which package of exam gloves has the lowest price per glove?

whyNot.0: $0.0849 per glove is the highest of the four.
whyNot.1: $0.082 per glove is close, but higher than the 250-pack's $0.07996.
whyNot.2: The biggest box works out to $0.083 per glove, more than the 250-pack.

A.q: An IV bag of 1.5 L is to run over 12 hours. What is the rate in milliliters per hour?

whyNot.0: 0.125 divides 1.5 by 12 without converting liters to milliliters; it is 0.125 L/h.
whyNot.1: 8 divides time by volume (12 ÷ 1.5), which inverts the rate.

A.q: A nurse counts 17 respirations in 30 seconds. At this rate, how many respirations per minute is that?
A.why: One minute is 2 × 30 seconds, so 17 × 2 = 34 respirations per minute.

whyNot.0: 51 multiplies by 3, the factor for a 20-second count.
whyNot.1: 8.5 divides by 2; a minute is longer than 30 seconds, so the count must grow.

B.q: Devon drives 90 miles to a clinical site at 60 mph and returns the same way at 45 mph. What is his average speed for the round trip? Round to the nearest tenth.
B.why: Time out: 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 h. Time back: 90 ÷ 45 = 2 h. Total: 180 miles in 3.5 h. 180 ÷ 3.5 = 51.43, about 51.4 mph.

whyNot.0: 52.5 mph averages the two speeds. He spends longer at 45 mph, so the true average is lower.
whyNot.2: 105 mph adds the two speeds together.
whyNot.3: 25.7 mph divides one-way distance (90) by the total time.

B.q: A pump delivers 2.5 mL of solution every minute. How many liters does it deliver in 4 hours?

whyNot.1: 6 L is a decimal slip: 600 mL is 0.6 L, not 6 L.
whyNot.2: 0.06 L divides 600 mL by 10,000 instead of 1,000.
whyNot.3: 0.01 L multiplies 2.5 by 4 hours (10 mL) without converting hours to minutes.

B.q: A courier drives 120 miles at an average speed of 48 miles per hour. How long does the trip take?
B.why: Time = distance ÷ rate = 120 ÷ 48 = 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes.

whyNot.0: 2 h 50 min reads 2.5 hours as 2 hours 50 minutes. Half an hour is 30 minutes.
whyNot.1: 2 h 24 min divides by 50 mph instead of 48 mph.
whyNot.2: 2 h 5 min reads the 0.5 hour as 5 minutes.

C.q: An IV of 1,200 mL is ordered over 10 hours. After 4 hours, 540 mL have infused. At what rate must the rest run to finish on time?
C.why: Left: 1,200 − 540 = 660 mL. Time left: 10 − 4 = 6 hours. Rate: 660 ÷ 6 = 110 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: 120 mL/h is the original rate (1,200 ÷ 10); the IV is ahead of schedule.
whyNot.1: 135 mL/h is the rate so far (540 ÷ 4).
whyNot.3: 165 mL/h divides the 660 mL left by the 4 hours already used.

C.q: A nursing student jogs 3 miles in 27 minutes, then walks 2 miles in 36 minutes. What is her average speed for the 5 miles? Round to the nearest tenth.
C.why: Total time: 27 + 36 = 63 minutes = 63/60 = 1.05 hours. Average speed: 5 ÷ 1.05 = 4.76, about 4.8 mph.

whyNot.0: 5.0 mph averages her two speeds (6.67 and 3.33 mph). She spends more time walking.
whyNot.3: 4.9 mph writes 1 hour 3 minutes as 1.03 hours.

C.q: Which pulse count shows the fastest heart rate?
C.why: Per minute: 29 × 3 = 87; 21 × 4 = 84; 40 × 2 = 80; 86. The 20-second count, 87 beats per minute, is fastest.

whyNot.2: 40 × 2 = 80 beats per minute; the largest count is not the fastest rate.
whyNot.3: 86 beats per minute is close, but 87 is faster.

reteach.title: The price tag on a deli counter
reteach.question: A deli shows '$6.80 per lb'. How does that one number let you price any order and compare any two shops?

blocks.h: A rate is the price of ONE
blocks.body: A deli sign gives the cost of one pound, so any order is just pounds × $6.80, and a $17 order bought 17 ÷ 6.80 = 2.5 lb. Every rate works like that sign: mL per hour, beats per minute, miles per hour. To compare two shops, put both signs in the same unit first. To find how long, divide by the sign; to find how much, multiply by it.

blocks.h: Same coffee, three shops, price per ounce

blocks.text: Before you compare, every price must be per the SAME unit. 1 lb is 16 oz, so $6.88 per lb is $0.43 per oz, not $6.88 per oz.

explain.body: Divide price by quantity to get the price for one unit, then compare like with like.

test.q: A 12-ounce bottle of hand sanitizer costs $4.20 and a 32-ounce bottle costs $10.24. How much less per ounce does the larger bottle cost?

whyNot.1: $0.32 is the larger bottle's unit price, not the difference.
whyNot.2: $6.04 is the difference in total price, not in price per ounce.
whyNot.3: $0.35 is the smaller bottle's unit price.

explain.body: Speed = distance ÷ time. Convert minutes to hours first (1 h 30 min = 1.5 h). For a whole trip, divide total distance by total time.

test.q: A cyclist rides 18 miles in 1 hour 30 minutes. What is her average speed?
test.why: 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours. 18 ÷ 1.5 = 12 miles per hour. Check: 12 × 1.5 = 18. ✓

whyNot.0: 13.8 reads 1 hour 30 minutes as 1.3 hours. Thirty minutes is half an hour, 0.5.
whyNot.1: 27 multiplies distance by time instead of dividing.
whyNot.2: 0.08 divides time by distance (1.5 ÷ 18), giving hours per mile.

explain.body: Turn the time into hours (or the rate's time unit), then multiply. 3 hours 24 minutes = 3 + 24/60 = 3.4 hours.

test.q: An IV runs at 125 mL per hour. How many milliliters infuse in 3 hours 24 minutes?
test.why: 24 minutes = 24/60 = 0.4 hour, so the time is 3.4 hours. 125 × 3.4 = 425 mL.

whyNot.0: 405 mL writes 3 hours 24 minutes as 3.24 hours.
whyNot.2: 375 mL uses 3 hours and leaves out the 24 minutes.
whyNot.3: 500 mL rounds the time up to 4 hours.

explain.body: Multiply a count by the number of those periods in a minute: × 4 for 15 seconds, × 3 for 20 seconds, × 2 for 30 seconds.

test.q: A nurse counts 19 heartbeats in 15 seconds. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
test.why: A minute holds four 15-second periods: 19 × 4 = 76 beats per minute.

whyNot.0: 38 multiplies by 2, the factor for a 30-second count.
whyNot.1: 57 multiplies by 3, the factor for a 20-second count.
whyNot.2: 285 multiplies by 15, the number of seconds counted.
